evidence: src/infrastructure/http/RequestReader.ts: RequestReader.requiredString delegates to optionalString, so the string-type check is written once. BadRequestError is the single input-error type.

src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: statusFor() is the only error-to-status mapping (ValidationError, BadRequestError and JSON parse errors give 400, NotFoundError gives 404, ConflictError gives 409, anything else gives 500).
src/infrastructure/http/createApp.ts: createApp() only builds the Express app, registers routes, the 404 fallback and errorHandler. It contains no error mapping or input parsing.
The graph shows the three controllers importing RequestReader, so input parsing is centralized and not reimplemented.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files serve one concern, the HTTP delivery adapter. RequestReader.ts turns untyped input into typed values and raises BadRequestError. createApp.ts wires the controllers, routes, 404 fallback and error handler. errorHandler.ts is the only place that maps errors to HTTP status codes. The status mapping lives in statusFor, so no rule is duplicated. Input validation lives in RequestReader, and the middleware reuses its BadRequestError instead of redefining it. Nothing in these files bypasses the module's abstractions. BadRequestError sits in RequestReader.ts rather than a separate errors file. That is a minor placement choice and not a cohesion failure.
